name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@988bb8b18e2d1a8a7cf59ae4dff7cb14b20fe0c5
    with:
      runtime_ref: 988bb8b18e2d1a8a7cf59ae4dff7cb14b20fe0c5

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@988bb8b18e2d1a8a7cf59ae4dff7cb14b20fe0c5
    with:
      runtime_ref: 988bb8b18e2d1a8a7cf59ae4dff7cb14b20fe0c5

      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}

      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}

    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}

Static HTML project. I'll build the game with plain HTML/CSS/JS and canvas. No framework needed. Need mobile touch controls, responsive. Should be visually impressive.

Game design: "Tom Taylor Car Chase" — 2D top-down GTA-like. Player on foot in a city, can steal cars (press E near car), drive to a house in the desert with police chase. Wanted level heat, police cars chase, ramming, roadblocks maybe. Desert house destination marked with arrow/minimap. On foot and driving.

Let me design a solid single-file-ish game with modular JS files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/game.js (or several modules)

Use canvas 2D with camera, world larger than viewport. Procedural city grid (roads, buildings) transitioning to desert. Player on foot; enter car with E/tap. Cars physics arcade: acceleration, steering, friction, drift. Cops spawn with wanted level, chase, ram. Health/damage. Goal: reach desert house at far east/south. Win screen.

Features:
- Title screen with name and controls.
- HUD: wanted stars, speed, mission arrow, minimap, health, objective.
- Mobile: virtual joystick for steering/movement, accelerate/brake buttons, action button for enter/exit car.
- Audio maybe simple WebAudio engine hum + siren synthesized. That adds polish. Keep optional with mute.
- Day/dusk desert gradient, sand texture, cacti, rocks, city buildings with shadows, road markings, streetlights.
- Particles: dust when drifting, sparks on collisions.
- Police AI: pursue using steering toward player, spawn near player when wanted, sirens; busted if cops close while on foot or car stopped? Simple: cops ram, contact drains health, wanted level rises when stealing a car / hitting cops / staying near. Goal distance ~ long.

Mission flow:
1. Start on foot outside a diner in city. Prompt: "Steal a car" - cars parked on streets with lock icons.
2. Steal car -> 2 stars wanted, cops dispatched. Objective: escape city and reach Tom Taylor's house in the desert (marked).
3. Drive along highway east/south. Cops chase, ram. Health car. If car destroyed, get out, steal another (cops continue).
4. Reach house zone -> mission complete screen with time, stars survived. Restart.

Maybe multiple phases: house location "Mojave" far away; arrow guidance. World: grid city near origin, highway leading east to desert house. Let's make world coordinate: city centered around (-600, 0)?? Simpler: world size 6000x6000, city region x from -1200 to 1200, desert to east from 1800 to 5000. Highway road at y=0 going east to house at x=4600, y=0? But cops chase and turns... City grid streets at every 400 units? Let's design:

World coordinates: 0..6400 x, 0..4800 y. City occupies x 300..2800, y 900..3900 with grid roads every 500 or so. Desert east: house at (5600, 2400). A main highway from city east edge to house, horizontal at y=2400, with some curves maybe straight. Player spawns in city around (1200, 2400) on foot near parked cars.

Camera smoothly follows, zoom scaling based on speed. Canvas renders in world units.

Road system: define roads as rectangles (horizontal/vertical). Collision: buildings are solid rectangles; roads free. Use spatial lists for buildings (only ~100). Render visible.

Simplify: build city blocks: roads at x positions and y positions. City origin: block grid 380 road width 120? blocks of buildings. City area 300..2900 x, 700..4100 y. Let's make grid cells 520, road width 110. Buildings inside blocks with margin 40, random subdivided lots. Some blocks are parks/parking lots. Cars parked along roads.

Highway: from city east edge (2900, 2400) to x 5900, width 220; desert house at (6250, 2400)? Let's use world width 6800, height 4800. House at (6250, 2400) with driveway, sand.

Cops: maintain array, spawn offscreen near player at road-ish positions (or just any position avoiding buildings), max 5. AI: steer toward player, accelerate; collision with buildings bounce. Use different vehicle colors (black/white police cars with lightbar). Sirens lights flashing.

Player on foot: walk, can be hit by cars -> health. Enter nearest car within 80 units. Cars: parked list with variety of shapes/colors; each car object with x,y,angle,speed, driver (none/player/cop). Stealing triggers cops. Player can exit car. Car health; cops damage.

Collision: AABB-ish oriented rectangles for cars vs buildings: use circle collision with building rectangles (car radius ~20). Cars vs cars simple circle push. Player vs buildings AABB/circle. Cars can drive over sidewalks and desert, slower offroad.

Wanted level: stars 1-5. On steal -> 2. Ramming cops +. Escaping reduces when out of sight? Keep simple: wanted stays, escalates over time if near cops. Goal is chase fun. Maybe add heat bar.

Health: player on foot 100; car health 100 shown. If car explodes -> player ejected with damage; cops continue. If player health 0 -> busted/wasted screen with retry.

Timers and score.

Minimap: top-right canvas or drawn in main canvas HUD; draw local area, roads as lines, house marker, cops dots. Use separate minimap canvas for crispness. Or draw into main canvas fixed overlay. Use DOM canvas overlay #minimap.

UI: HUD DOM overlay with CSS (mission text, stars, speedometer, health), nice typography. Title overlay with start button. Mobile joystick.

Touch controls: left joystick (steering / walking), right buttons: GAS, BRAKE, and action (E). For driving, joystick x controls steer, gas/brake for speed; or joystick full direction? Natural: joystick for steer (left/right), gas/brake buttons. On foot: joystick moves in any direction and gas not needed. Buttons adapt labels: "STEAL"/"EXIT". Add handbrake button maybe. On mobile driving: gas hold + steer. Good.

Keyboard: WASD/arrows, Space handbrake, E enter/exit, Shift? Nitro maybe not. Add R restart. M mute.

Visual polish: 
- Title screen with animated background (canvas game rendering paused with cops? Or CSS gradient + car silhouette). Better: game renders attract mode behind overlay (slow camera pan over city) - but complexity. Simple: show canvas world at spawn with cops? I'll render the game in background paused, overlay gradient. Nice.
- Fonts: Google fonts can't rely offline? Use system fonts with fallback; maybe embed a Google Fonts link (network available when user opens). Use 'Bebas Neue'/'Inter' with fallback. Offline-first: CSS font stack impact-ish (Haettenschweiler, 'Arial Narrow Bold'). Nice GTA vibe with orange/black.
- Screen shake on collisions.
- Sun/dusk lighting in desert with long shadows.
- Dust particles, tire skid marks (store and fade).
- Sirens audio via WebAudio oscillators, engine hum. Must start after user gesture.
- Speed lines / camera zoom.
- Wanted stars flash.

Let me plan code architecture:

index.html — canvas #game, HUD elements, overlays, mobile controls, script type=module src=js/main.js.

Files:
- js/main.js: bootstrap, loop, input wiring, state screens.
- js/world.js: world generation, roads/buildings/props, collision helpers, rendering static world ground + objects.
- js/entities.js: player, cars, cops, particles, skid marks.
- js/render.js maybe.
- js/audio.js: synth engine/siren.
- styles.css.

Keep manageable ~1500-2200 lines total. Should be robust.

Let me think about the game loop and physics carefully.

Coordinate system: world units where player car ~ 46 length, 24 width; on foot radius 9. Speed units per second. Car max ~ 520 units/s (~31 mph visually? scale arbitrary). City blocks 520 units. Should feel fast but controllable. Camera zoom ~0.9 desktop.

Canvas CSS size fills viewport; internal size = css * dpr; use transform scale for zoom.

World:
const WORLD = {w: 7200, h: 4800}.
City: x: 400..3200, y: 700..4100.
Block grid step 520, road width 120. Blocks: for cx from 400 to 3200 step 520, etc. Actually roads at grid lines. Let's define cityCols = 5, rows = 6 => block size 520. City rect x0=400,y0=700, x1=3200,y1=4100 (2800 x 3400). With grid step 500? Let's produce roads at each grid line and blocks between.

Simpler: generate roads as lines list:
vertical roads at x = 400 + i*560 for i=0..5 (city width 2800), horizontal roads at y = 700 + j*566 for j=0..6 (3400/6). Buildings in cells between roads, with road half-width 60.

For each cell (between adjacent roads), create building(s) inset 85 from road centers. Each cell ~500x506; split into 1-4 buildings randomly with gap, heights (2.5D fake via shadow + rooftop color offset). Solid collision rect.

Some cells become parks (trees), parking lots with parked cars, or plazas. Ensure spawn block near (1200, 2400) has a parking lot with cars. We'll hardcode spawn at a road near diner.

Main highway: from city right edge x=3200 to house x=6300 at y=2400, width 260. Also maybe a desert road with slight curve? Straight is fine, add billboards and telephone poles, cacti, rocks. Need ensure no buildings block highway. City ends at x=3200.

Desert house at x=6250, y=2400. A fenced yard, house, pool? Car must reach driveway zone (radius 130). Add "TOM TAYLOR'S HOUSE" sign. World edge beyond.

Goal marker big arrow and beam.

Police spawn: when wanted>0, spawn cop cars at distance 900-1300 from player in random direction, checking no building collision (try several points; if on building, skip). Cop AI: 
- target = player pos.
- desired angle to target; steer toward, but avoid buildings via simple ray feelers: check point ahead; if inside building, steer offset.
- speed up to 430-520 depending on wanted.
- If distance < 60, ram.
- Cop cars collide with buildings -> damage them, bounce.
- Cop cars collide with player car -> damage both, screen shake, wanted + heat.
- Cops on foot? No, cops stay in cars.
- Cops shoot? Maybe not; health drained by rams. Could add "busted" if player on foot and cop within 40 for 2 sec. Let's add busted meter: on foot near cop -> busted quickly. In car near stationary cops? Keep car ramming.

Wanted escalation: initial 2 stars. Every 25 sec chase maybe +star up to 5? Add more cops with higher stars. Could be annoying. Instead stars increase when you damage cops, decrease when far (not implemented). Mission is short (~60-90s), fine.

Stealing: nearest car within 95 and on foot => prompt. Press E/action -> player enters; car color; wanted=2; siren starts; "STOLEN!" flash. If you steal another car while in car? Exit first. Cars can be any including cop cars? Maybe allow stealing cop car? Fun but complexity; skip, cops locked.

On foot: speed 190, animation legs simple. Player can be run over by cop cars -> damage.

Car physics:
state: x,y,angle (facing), vx,vy or speed along heading + lateral. Arcade:
- input throttle (1 forward, -1 reverse/brake), steer (-1..1), handbrake.
- speed scalar along forward: accel 480/s^2 forward, max 520 (or 620 with boost on highway? maybe 600). reverse max -180.
- drag: speed *= 0.995^... use friction decel 180/s when no throttle, rolling.
- angle += steer * turnRate * (speed/max) * dt * direction sign. turnRate ~ 2.4 rad/s.
- drift: maintain velocity vector and blend toward forward. Simpler kinematic with drift factor: vx = lerp(vx, forwardX*speed, grip). Use velocity vector approach:
  - forward = (cos a, sin a)
  - engine force along forward; velocity += forward*accel*dt
  - lateral velocity damped strongly: vLat *= exp(-grip*dt) with grip 8 normal, 2.5 handbrake.
  - speed clamp.
  - angle steering scaled by forward speed; handbrake adds rotation.
This yields nice drift. Implement:
```
const fwd = {x: cos, y: sin};
const right = {x:-sin, y:cos};
let vF = vx*fwd.x + vy*fwd.y;
let vR = vx*right.x + vy*right.y;
vF += throttle*accel*dt;
vF -= vF*drag*dt... 
vF = clamp(vF, -maxReverse, max);
vR *= Math.exp(-grip*dt);
angle += steer * turnSpeed * dt * clamp(Math.abs(vF)/200,0,1) * Math.sign(vF||1);
vx = fwd.x*vF + right.x*vR; ...
```
Rotate fwd after angle update ideally. fine.

Offroad friction: determine if car center on road (any road rect) or desert; if offroad, max speed lower (0.55) and dust particles.

Collision with buildings: circle-vs-rect resolve; kill velocity component, damage based on impact. Car radius 18. Use swept-ish substeps if speed high; with dt clamped 1/30, speed 600 => 20 units/frame, okay vs 120 roads. Solid.

Player on foot collision: circle vs buildings, slide.

Camera: follow with lerp, zoom based on speed: base 0.95 scaled by min(canvas dims). Need responsive zoom: on mobile portrait, zoom maybe 0.7 to see enough. Compute zoom = clamp(min(w,h)/900, 0.55, 1.05) then reduce slightly when fast. Actually world units: car 46 long; on 900px height, visible 900/0.9=1000 units. Good.

Canvas transform: ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0); then translate(w/2,h/2), scale(zoom), translate(-cam.x,-cam.y).

Rendering:
- ground: city asphalt/sidewalk base color; big ground fill by region: city concrete #3a3f46? Desert sand #c9a56a. Roads dark.
- Draw desert sand base whole world, then city base rect lighter concrete with slight texture (deterministic random dots limited?). Use offscreen pattern canvases for noise: create 128px pattern for sand and asphalt and sidewalk. Patterns with transform under camera would need translation alignment; pattern is in current transform coordinates so fine.
- Roads: draw rects fill #2b2d31, lane markers dashed yellow/white. Sidewalk borders.
- Buildings: draw shadows offset (sun top-left => shadow bottom-right), body fill with palette (browns, grays, teal), rooftop inset, windows grid. High enough count (~80) but only visible ones drawn. Add AC units? Keep.
- Parks: green rect with trees circles.
- Parking lots with cars.
- Desert props: cacti, rocks, bushes, telephone poles along highway, billboards, tumbleweed maybe.
- House: big villa with driveway, palm trees, pool, fence, neon sign "TOM TAYLOR".
- Goal: pulsing circle + arrow at top of screen (HUD arrow computed).
- Cars: rounded rectangles with roof, windows, headlights, wheels; police with light bar flashing red/blue, "POLICE" maybe. Player car highlight.

Particles: dust circles, sparks, explosion. Skid marks array of segments fade.

Audio: WebAudio engine oscillator sawtooth with lowpass, frequency by speed, gain low; siren alternating two tones when wanted>0; crash noise; pick-up blip. Mute toggle.

HUD DOM:
- Top-left: mission label "MISSION" + objective text; star row.
- Top-right minimap canvas 150x150 with border.
- Bottom-right: speedometer dial? Use DOM numeric + bar; mobile controls overlap. Keep speed + car health bars bottom center.
- Off-screen arrow indicator: draw in canvas maybe DOM. Draw on main canvas as screen-space marker pointing to goal when off-screen. Easier draw after world transform reset.

Overlays:
- Start screen: title "TOM TAYLOR" big, "CAR CHASE", tagline, controls, START button. Mobile shows touch controls hint.
- Messages: toast "CAR STOLEN", "POLICE DISPATCHED", "WRONG WAY?" etc.
- End screen: "MISSION COMPLETE" with time/stars; "WASTED" with retry.

Implementation detail: state machine 'title','playing','complete','wasted'. Start button begins. On title, render world idle and camera slow pan. Pause on visibility.

Input: keyboard set; touch joystick with pointer events; buttons pointerdown/up. Touch only show if coarse pointer or touch detected; add toggles. Also allow mobile always visible on small screens. Detect `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` and show.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D top-down GTA-like game called “Tom Taylor Car Chase” where the player steals cars, is chased by police, and reaches a house in the desert.
- No clarifying questions; reasonable assumptions should be made.

## Requirements
- Game must include car theft, police chase gameplay, and a desert house destination.
- Complete and playable, not a prototype.
- Mobile support required by repo conventions: responsive layout, usable touch controls, safe areas, no browser gesture conflicts.
- Use browser verification screenshots; reject blank/loading canvases.

## Decisions
- Plain static HTML/CSS/JS with Canvas 2D; no framework or build step.
- World: city grid (`CITY` ~420–3140 × 720–4040) connected to a long eastbound highway at `HIGHWAY_Y ≈ 2380`, leading to a desert villa at `GOAL {x:11760,y:2190,r:125}`.
- Game flow: start on foot outside parked cars → steal a car (`E` / touch action) → 2-star wanted level and police dispatch → reach gold house marker → mission complete.
- Player can exit/re-steal cars; car damage, explosions, wrrecked cops, on-foot bust timer, wasted/busted endings, restart.
- Mobile touch: left virtual joystick + GAS/BRAKE/DRIFT + STEAL/EXIT action; keyboard WASD/arrows, Space drift, E action, R restart, M mute.
- Synthesised WebAudio engine/siren/crash/win-loss sounds, no external audio assets.
- Added debug handle `window.__ttcc` for QA (`state`, `teleport`, `giveCar`, `startGame`, `triggerEnd`, etc.).

## Work State

### Completed
- `index.html` with title screen, HUD, minimap, toast, touch controls, end screen, favicon.
- `styles.css` with full responsive desktop/mobile/landscape styling and safe-area handling.
- `js/world.js`: seeded city generation, roads/crosswalks/buildings/parks/lots, parked-car spots, highway, desert props, telephone wires, billboards, detailed villa/pool/fence/arch, goal marker drawing.
- `js/audio.js`: synthesised engine, siren, crash, blips, win/lose stings, mute.
- `js/main.js`: vehicle physics with drift/handbrake/offroad handling, car entry/exit, police AI with wall avoidance/stuck recovery, rubber-banding, highway-aware cop spawning, damage, wrecks, particles, skid marks, dust, minimap, HUD, goal arrow, title/end flow.
- Verified in browser via `playwright-cli`: title, gameplay, stealing, driving, highway, house, win screen, wasted screen, desktop HUD.
- Verified mobile portrait (390×844) and landscape (844×390) layouts; fixed touch controls, action button, vehicle panel placement.
- Fixed major bug: `.touch` CSS class matched `<body class="touch">` and hid the whole body; scoped to `#touch`.
- Fixed end screen hidden-class bug; win/wasted overlays now render.
- Server running in tmux session `game` at `http://localhost:3000` via `PORT=3000 ./start.sh`.
- Changes are uncommitted in git.

### Active
- Final gameplay/visual balancing after latest edits to police highway spawning/rubber-banding and off-screen goal label background plate.
- Need re-verify after these last edits: syntax, desktop chase with highway-spawned cops, mobile landscape vehicle panel position, and end screens.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check js/main.js` and reload the game; verify no console/runtime errors.
2. Test highway chase with new cop spawning: steal car, teleport/highway drive, confirm cops spawn on highway and remain in the chase.
3. Re-test mobile landscape layout after moving the touch vehicle panel to top-center; confirm no overlap with minimap/sound button or controls.
4. Re-check complete/wasted end screens and restart button after latest changes.
5. Optionally improve balance/HUD polish; then remove QA screenshots if desired and report assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure, HUD, title/end screens, touch controls, favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all visual styling and responsive/touch/landscape layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: game loop, physics, AI, stealing, HUD, rendering, debug handle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: procedural world/city/highway/desert/house generation and drawing.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesised audio engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: QA screenshots including title, gameplay, mobile, win, wasted.

## Important Context
- Playwright `resize` command breaks page layout (body becomes `display:none`/0×0); use `playwright-cli run-code "async (page) => { await page.setViewportSize({width:...,height:...}); }"` instead.
- Use `playwright-cli open --mobile` or viewport sizing then reload to exercise true mobile touch detection (`innerWidth<820` also enables touch).
- Rendered/verified URLs: `http://localhost:3000`.
- Last edits to main.js: `spawnCop` now spawns on the highway when the player is on it; `updateCops` adds rubber-banding via `catchUp`; off-screen goal label now has a dark background plate.
- CSS now scopes touch section as `#touch` and uses `body.touch #touch { display: block; }`.
- Global rule `[hidden] { display:none !important; }` is important for hidden HUD/screens.
- Debug QA teleport does not immediately update `state.player.x/y` while in a car; player syncs next frame.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
